category_title: Disengaged EMLLs with antsy behavior and coping through imitation
minimal_context: Shen is sitting at his desk in the general classroom during instructional time to complete his assigned written work.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for instructional time. Please look at the assigned work on your desk and begin.

STUDENT: (Sits quietly at first and watches the other students, trying to follow their actions.)

TUTOR: Go ahead and read the instructions on the paper.

STUDENT: (Looks at the English words on the page, then becomes antsy and starts shifting around in his seat.)

TUTOR: You need to do the assignment. What do you think you should do next?

STUDENT: I don’t understand, so I won’t do it. (Gets up out of his seat and begins walking around the classroom without permission.)

options.A: Request clarification from the student by asking for explanations and elaborations about the assigned written work.
options.B: Provide person-to-person home language support to the student to help with the assigned written work.
options.C: Send a clear message to the student regarding dissatisfaction with their out-of-seat behavior during the task.
options.D: Quickly redirect the student to the assigned written work and emphasize the importance of staying focused.
